entry.title: Introduction to the Loki Stack: Lightweight Logging for Kubernetes
entry.summary:
What is the Loki Stack?
Loki Stack is a lightweight, cloud‑native logging system built with the same design philosophy as Prometheus. It’s a great fit for Kubernetes environments because it keeps things simple, scalable, and cost‑effective — all of which matter a lot in modern DevOps workflows. Unlike traditional logging tools that index the entire log content, Loki takes a smarter approach: it indexes only the metadata labels. Logs themselves are stored as compressed streams. This makes Loki far more efficient and cheaper to run compared to systems like Elasticsearch. The core engine. It handles log ingestion, storage, and querying. Components like the Distributor, Ingester, and Querier work together to push logs, compress them, store them (often in S3 or GCS), and make them searchable.…
